title: Ashoka Young Changemakers
description: A selective fellowship-style network (not a single event or competition) for young social entrepreneurs who have already originated an idea, built a team, and demonstrated real-world impact. A 4-stage process (online nomination, national review, international review, in-person selection panel) leads to induction into Ashoka's global changemaker network with mentorship, media partnerships and reimbursed travel to the selection panel.
residency_restrictions: Applicants may only apply to AYC in their country of residence; the program is currently recruiting only in the 6 countries listed above. Residents of any other country (including Turkey and all European countries) are explicitly NOT currently eligible and are told to contact their local Ashoka country office for other youth opportunities instead.
application_requirements: an original idea already acted on
selectivity_evidence: 4-stage selection process (online nomination -> national review -> international review -> in-person selection panel including social entrepreneurs and journalists) — genuinely selective, though no published acceptance rate found. Selectivity_tier not asserted numerically without one.
verification_status: Verified - fetched directly via browser (not WebFetch, which returned 403 on this domain on the first attempt) on 2026-08-22. Nominations stated as accepted year-round; the 6 currently-recruiting countries are the program's own explicit list.
notes: IMPORTANT MISMATCH WITH THIS RESEARCH PASS'S WEIGHTING: this program does not currently serve Turkey or Europe at all -- it is included because it is a genuine, well-verified fellowship (a category with zero prior rows) that serves ORYN's existing US user base, not because it fits the Turkey/Europe brief. An earlier lead (an ashoka.org/en-tr Turkish-language page existing) turned out NOT to mean Turkey has an active AYC cohort -- verified the actual recruiting-country list directly rather than inferring eligibility from a localized page existing, per the standing rule to verify identity/scope rather than pattern-match.
